filing_meta.note: Pre-BlueHalo vintage. Score against FY22 narrative as filed.

extraction_notes: Filing names trademarked product lines (Switchblade, Raven, Wasp, Puma, Quantix, VAPOR, Arcturus UAV, Crysalis, Jump) but does NOT name Pentagon Program Elements (PE numbers) or specific named DoD programs of record in the form 'AFRL Quantum Networking' / 'SDA Tracking Layer'. The bulk of forward-looking narrative is segment-level (Small UAS / MUAS / TMS / UGV / HAPS) and customer-level (Army, SOCOM, Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, SoftBank). For this cohort, the J-Book pattern is INHERENTLY LOW DENSITY in this filing: AVAV at this vintage sells via Family of Systems IDIQs, not via line-item-named PEs. We extract claims at the granularity the filing supports: product-line revenue claims (Switchblade as TMS product-of-record candidate; Puma/Raven sUAS programs), customer concentration claims (Army 21%, SoftBank 9%, HAPSMobile 1%, foreign 32%), and the HAPS/SoftBank development narrative.

claims.claim_text: AVAV's TMS segment is anchored by the Switchblade tactical missile family, sold to U.S. DoD organizations including Army and SOCOM; the company expects continued long-term growth in TMS adoption by the U.S. military.
claims.subject: AeroVironment Tactical Missile Systems / Switchblade
claims.predicate: is a Pentagon-funded loitering munition product line with forward growth narrative
claims.object_value: TMS segment growth driven by Switchblade sales to Army/SOCOM
claims.source_quote: We supply unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), tactical missile systems (TMS), unmanned ground vehicles (UGV) and related services primarily to organizations within the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) ... We have many U.S. registered trademarks including those for AeroVironment, AV, Switchblade, Raven, Wasp, Quantix, VAPOR, Arcturus UAV, Crysalis and Jump ... We intend to ... increase the penetration of our TMS within the U.S. military and within the military forces of allied nations.

claims.claim_text: AVAV's small UAS product family (Raven, Puma, Wasp, Blackwing) is the leading small UAS line for the U.S. military and is expected to continue driving small UAS revenue.
claims.subject: AeroVironment small UAS (Raven RQ-11, Puma RQ-20, Wasp, Blackwing)
claims.predicate: is the program-of-record small-UAS family for U.S. Army and other services with forward demand
claims.object_value: Continued sUAS revenue from Army Family of Systems
claims.source_quote: Our small UAS and medium UAS (MUAS), TMS and UGV enjoy leading positions in their respective markets. We intend to increase the penetration of our small UAS and MUAS and UGV products and services within the U.S. military ... we generated approximately 21% of our revenue from the U.S. Army.

claims.claim_text: AVAV's medium UAS (MUAS) segment is anchored by the Arcturus JUMP 20 and T-20 platforms (acquired Feb 2021); the company expects MUAS to be a growth pillar in U.S. and allied markets.
claims.subject: AeroVironment MUAS / Arcturus JUMP 20 / T-20
claims.predicate: is positioned as the FTUAS-class medium UAS program with forward DoD pipeline
claims.object_value: MUAS growth from Future Tactical UAS competition and Army demand
claims.source_quote: Our small UAS and medium UAS (MUAS), TMS and UGV enjoy leading positions in their respective markets ... MUAS: Petaluma, CA and Rohnert Park, CA. ... Arcturus revenue and loss from operations for the year ended April 30, 2021 since acquisition on February 19, 2021 was $15,837,000 and $1,869,000.

claims.claim_text: 21% of AVAV's FY2022 revenue came from the U.S. Army (placed on behalf of itself and other DoD orgs); 55% from DoD overall; 66% from U.S. government as prime or subcontractor including foreign military sales.
claims.subject: AVAV DoD/Army revenue concentration
claims.predicate: constitutes the majority of revenue, with implied forward dependence on continued DoD appropriations for sUAS/TMS/MUAS
claims.object_value: Army 21%, DoD 55%, USG total 66% of FY22 revenue
claims.source_quote: During our fiscal year ended April 30, 2022, we generated approximately 21% of our revenue from the U.S. Army ... Other U.S. government agencies and government subcontractors accounted for 37% of our sales revenue ... Sales to the U.S. government, either as a prime contractor or subcontractor and inclusive of foreign military sales, represented approximately 66% of our revenue for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2022. The DoD, our principal U.S. government customer, accounted for approximately 55%.

claims.claim_text: AVAV's HAPS (High Altitude Pseudo-Satellite / Sunglider) program with SoftBank generated $43.3M in FY22 revenue (about 10% of total) under a Master Design and Development Agreement that SoftBank can terminate at convenience; this is a key forward design-and-development revenue stream.
claims.subject: AVAV HAPS / Sunglider with SoftBank
claims.predicate: is a material commercial-program revenue stream with stated termination-at-convenience risk
claims.object_value: $43.3M FY22 HAPS revenue; ~10% of total; counterparty SoftBank/HAPSMobile
claims.source_quote: In May 2021, we and HAPSMobile mutually agreed to terminate our Design and Development Agreement and we entered into a Master Design and Development Agreement with SoftBank ... The Company recorded revenue under both the MDDA and DDA and preliminary design agreements between the Company and SoftBank of $43,325,000, $42,426,000 and $60,864,000 for the fiscal years ended April 30, 2022, 2021 and 2020 ... The Master Design and Development Agreement allows SoftBank to terminate the contract at its convenience for any reason.

claims.claim_text: AVAV's UGV segment (Telerob acquisition, May 2021) is positioned to expand the company's U.S. and allied military / public-safety footprint with EOD/CBRN remote-controlled ground robots.
claims.subject: AeroVironment UGV / Telerob
claims.predicate: is a new segment with stated growth narrative into DoD and allied EOD/CBRN markets
claims.object_value: Telerob acquired May 3, 2021; FY22 Telerob revenue $29.2M, loss $12.1M; net cash purchase $46.2M
claims.source_quote: On May 3, 2021, the Company closed its acquisition of Telerob pursuant to the terms of the Telerob Purchase Agreement. Telerob develops, manufactures, sells, and services remote-controlled unmanned ground robots and transport vehicles for civil and defense applications ... Telerob revenue and loss from operations for the year ended April 30, 2022 since acquisition on May 3, 2021 was $29,177,000 and $12,115,000.
